newsitem.title: USA: Baa muni bonds continue to outperform Aaa paper.
newsitem.headline: Baa muni bonds continue to outperform Aaa paper.

text.p: Spreads between Aaa and Baa-rated municipals continued to narrow last week, figures from Delphis Hanover Corp show.
From June 6 to the June 13, spreads on 30-year Baa paper improved by 20 basis points, while spreads on comparable Aaa paper improved by just 10 basis points.
The disparity was even more apparent from 2004 through 2009, where non-rated paper improved by 25 basis points versus 10 basis points of improvement in comparable Aaa paper.

Delphis Hanover president Austin Tobin said when 30-year, Aaa muni yields dip below 80 percent of U.S. Treasury bond yields, and remain there for a week or so, a correction has traditionally followed. The ratio stood at 79.5 percent Friday, just above the new 52-week low of 79.0 set June 10.
In addition, a scenario where lesser bonds continue to improve while Aaa bonds remain constant, has signaled potential trouble in the past, he said.
"A good risk commitment manager...in a situation like this would be telling his traders 'Let's lighten up fellas, lighten up quite a bit in here, and see what happens next,'" Tobin said.
A municipal trader said one reason lesser quality bonds have shown more improvement than high-grade issues is because buyers are hunting for yield.

"You've got mutual funds who have a lot of bonds getting called, but they have no new cash," the trader said. "And they have bonds that they bought 10 years ago when yields were 7.0 or 8.0 percent, and they need to replace with the highest yielding thing possible because their dividend will get cut otherwise."

While portfolio managers know it doesn't make sense to buy an AMT housing bond at 50 basis points off high-grades when they used to buy it at 80 basis points off, they do it anyway in pursuit of yield, he said.
"You know it's going to get you in the end, but it's going to lessen the blow on your dividend," he said.
